classes.desc: Fixed-capacity cache with least-recently-used eviction backed by an OrderedDict.
classes.name: LRUCache

data_flow_ascii:
seeded key stream -> get/put -> OrderedDict (recency order)
over-capacity put -> popitem(last=False) evicts LRU key
hits/misses/evictions -> stats() -> printed trace + summary
description_sentence: A fixed-capacity LRU cache that evicts the least-recently-used entry and reports hit, miss, and eviction statistics.
failure_note: Capacity below 1 raises ValueError at construction; get() on a missing key returns None instead of raising.

label: LRU cache
output_shape: Prints a per-operation trace (step, op, key, hit/miss/evicted) plus the final MRU-ordered cache and hit-rate summary.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that evicts the least-recently-used entry on overflow and tracks hit rates to show how well it performs.

qa.a: An OrderedDict keeps keys in access order; get() and put() call move_to_end() so the front is always the least-recently-used key.
The new entry is added, then popitem(last=False) removes the front (LRU) entry and the eviction counter increments.
qa.q: What happens on a put when the cache is full?

qa.a: No locking is included; it is designed for single-threaded use or external synchronization.

resume_bullet_template: Implemented a {topic} in Python on an OrderedDict with O(1) get/put and hit/miss/eviction instrumentation.
run_notes: --capacity, --lookups, and --key-space override the demo configuration from @@TOPIC_PARAMS@@.
scaling_note: Single-process structure; capacity is bounded by RAM and there is no sharding or cross-process sharing.
storage_note: In-memory only: the cache and its counters live in the process and vanish on exit; no disk persistence.
tradeoff_note: OrderedDict gives simple O(1) LRU ordering at the cost of per-entry overhead versus a plain dict with manual timestamps.
